study type: Secondary analysis of a multicenter 3-arm double-blind randomized controlled trial
exposure: antibiotic receipt (per hospital protocols or physician discretion)
outcome: maternal peripartum infection (composite of chorioamnionitis, endometritis, sepsis, wound infection/abscess)
cohort: The study participants were 652 high-risk laboring term pregnant patients in Cameroon with prolonged labor or rupture of membranes, who were originally enrolled in an antibiotic prophylaxis trial.
finding: A predictive model, moderately predictive of maternal peripartum infection, included education level, antibiotic indication, and cesarean birth as independently associated factors among high-risk laboring patients in Cameroon.
mod_finding: Cesarean birth was independently associated with an increased risk of maternal peripartum infection.
